about.title: About 15 vs 30 Year Mortgage Calculator - Mortgage Term Comparison Tool
about.description: The 15 vs 30 Year Mortgage Calculator is a comprehensive comparison tool designed to help homebuyers analyze the financial differences between 15-year and 30-year mortgage terms. This calculator provides side-by-side comparisons of monthly payments, total interest costs, and long-term savings to help you make informed decisions about mortgage term selection. Whether you're purchasing a home or refinancing, understanding the trade-offs between shorter and longer mortgage terms is crucial for optimizing your home financing strategy.

faq.q: What's the main difference between 15-year and 30-year mortgages?
faq.a: 15-year mortgages have higher monthly payments but lower interest rates and total interest costs. 30-year mortgages offer lower monthly payments but higher total interest over the loan term. The choice depends on your budget and financial priorities.

faq.q: How much can I save with a 15-year mortgage?
faq.a: 15-year mortgages typically save $100,000-$200,000+ in total interest compared to 30-year loans. For example, a $300,000 loan might cost $150,000 in interest (15-year) vs $320,000 (30-year), saving $170,000.

faq.q: Should I choose a 15-year or 30-year mortgage?
faq.a: Choose 15-year if you can afford higher payments and want to build equity faster. Choose 30-year if you need lower payments, want investment flexibility, or prefer more disposable income for other financial goals.

faq.q: Can I pay off a 30-year mortgage early like a 15-year?
faq.a: Yes, you can make extra principal payments on a 30-year mortgage to pay it off faster. This provides flexibility to reduce payments during tight months while still achieving faster payoff when possible.
